title: Speonk (Neck, River, and Village)
summary: A Native name for the Speonk neck, river and village landscape; its precise translation remains uncertain.
introduction_content: Speonk names a neck, river and present-day village near the western edge of Southampton. The name preserves a Native geographic reference within a landscape later described through meadow allotments, roads and settlements. Tooker, pp. 248–249
history_content: Tooker cites a 1712 Southampton record for meadow and upland at Speonk. His entry is also unusually candid about uncertainty: he considers more than one explanation and does not settle the name’s derivation. Retaining that uncertainty respects the difference between a recorded Indigenous name and a later scholar’s attempt to interpret it. Tooker, pp. 248–249
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Speeunk, Speunk, Speonk, and Waspeunk. Tooker explicitly left the derivation in doubt, discussing both elevated ground and a possible stream-margin reading. Neither is presented here as a settled translation.

Why Place Names Matter

“Using Indigenous names instead of the English alternatives helps to reclaim Indigenous land stewardship, document Indigenous knowledge, and exhibits local Indigenous identity.”

— Dehrich A. Schmidt-Chya, Qikertarmiut Nunat Apertaarait Anirturluki: Preserving the Indigenous Place Names of the Kodiak Archipelago (2020), Abstract, PDF page iii

The recorded spellings are historical evidence; the competing English interpretations are Tooker’s scholarly proposals. Tooker, pp. 248–249
preservation_content: Speonk is a continuing Long Island placename where village, river, meadow, and neck names carry older Indigenous geography into modern maps.
whereintheworld_content: The pin locates the present village of Speonk as a general reference. Tooker associated the older name with a neck and river east of Seatuck and the town boundary. It is not an exact historic settlement point, and the village, river and neck should not be treated as identical boundaries. Tooker, pp. 248–249
